chunks: My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us from al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq al-Nahdi, from al-Husayn ibn Ulwan, from Amr ibn Thabit, from his father, from Sa'd ibn Turayf, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said one day on the pulpit of Kufa: I am the Master of the Successors and the Successor of the Master of the Prophets. I am the Imam of the Muslims, the Leader of the Pious, the Master of the Believers, and the husband of the Mistress of the Women of the Worlds. I am the one who wears a ring on the right hand, and whose forehead is dusty [from prostration]. I am the one who made the two migrations, and who gave the two pledges of allegiance. I am the patron of Badr and Hunayn. I am the one who strikes with two swords, and who charges on two horses. I am the inheritor of the knowledge of the former peoples, and the Proof of God over humanity after the prophets and Muhammad ibn Abdullah (may God's blessings be upon him and his family), the Seal of the Prophets. My allies will receive mercy, and my enemies are damned.

And indeed, my beloved, the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family), would frequently say to me: O Ali, loving you is God-consciousness and faith, and hating you is disbelief and hypocrisy. And I am the House of Wisdom, and you are its key. Whoever claims to love me while hating you is a liar.

key_terms.بيت الحكمة: House of Wisdom -- metaphor for the Prophet as the repository of divine wisdom
key_terms.حجة الله: Proof of God -- one whose existence serves as evidence of divine guidance for humanity
key_terms.سيد الوصيين: Master of the Successors -- title affirming his supreme position among all prophetic legatees
key_terms.مفتاحه: Its key -- metaphor for Ali as the one who unlocks access to prophetic wisdom

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about himself on the pulpit of Kufa?
ai.summary: In this famous sermon delivered on the pulpit of Kufa, Imam Ali (AS) proclaimed his unique station and virtues in Islam. He enumerated his titles -- Master of Successors, Imam of Muslims, Leader of the Pious, patron of Badr and Hunayn, inheritor of prophetic knowledge, and Proof of God after the prophets. He concluded by quoting the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) who declared that love for Ali is an expression of faith while hatred of him is a sign of disbelief and hypocrisy. This sermon, addressed to the people of Kufa during Imam Ali's caliphate, was meant to remind his community of his divinely appointed authority in a period when his leadership was being challenged.
word_analysis: the one who wears a ring
